name: Farshad Khorrami
title: Professor; Director, Control/Robotics Research Laboratory
fitReason: CRRL combines substantial current embodied-AI policy research with a physical robotics lab. This is a stronger match through the world-model and visual-imitation projects than through the broader nonlinear-control/cybersecurity portfolio.

physicalEvidence.summary: DexWM, revised March 16, 2026, optimizes Franka Panda/Allegro actions with a learned human-video world model. It reports 10 successful grasps in 12 trials over four objects, executing optimized two-step actions open-loop; reach/place benchmarks are simulation. Lead author Raktim Goswami remains a CRRL PhD student, but the paper explicitly states that this work was done during his Meta internship, and his page identifies Yann LeCun as that internship mentor. CRRL separately lists Franka and dexterous-hand equipment; the inspected sources do not link that inventory to these specific trials. Treat the study as collaborative hardware with location, ownership and visitor access unresolved.

shortVisit.summary: The full current Join page accepts PhD applications and specifically welcomes current NYU master’s/undergraduate students. It also has postdoc inquiries. No external short-term master’s visitor invitation is stated; local thesis opportunities receive no visitor credit.

scoreReasons.fit: Strong current world-model manipulation within a broader control/security group.
scoreReasons.physical: Physical DexWM execution is verified in a Meta–NYU collaboration conducted during the lead author’s Meta internship. CRRL student membership and a separate equipment inventory do not establish where these trials ran or independent current visitor access; cap at 20.
scoreReasons.shortVisit: Current local-master’s wording does not invite external summer visitors.
scoreReasons.freshness: March 2026 revised physical source and June 2026 own-group methods paper.
